stories.title: Man Stabbed in Abdomen and Robbed of Cellphone in Flushing; Two Arrested
stories.dek: A 31-year-old man was stabbed and robbed of his phone near 37th Avenue in Flushing, and police arrested two people in connection with the robbery, Hoodline reported.
body: A 31-year-old man was stabbed multiple times in the abdomen and robbed of his cellphone on a Flushing street in the early morning hours of Oct. 1, according to Hoodline.

The attack happened near 109-15 37th Avenue in Queens, Hoodline reported. Citing News 12, the outlet said the robbery took place shortly after 2 a.m.; another account cited in the article placed it at about 2:10 a.m.

According to News 12's account as cited by Hoodline, four people approached the man, displayed a cutting instrument, stabbed him and took his phone. Hoodline noted that other accounts differed, with one describing a single attacker and another saying police were seeking three suspects. Those discrepancies had not been resolved, the outlet said.
The man was taken to New York-Presbyterian Queens Hospital, according to News 12. His current condition was not reported.

Police arrested Mateo Tonato, 20, and Scarleth Remache, 19, in connection with the robbery, according to the report. Both face assault and robbery charges, News 12 reported. The charges are accusations, and both are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

sources.title: Man Stabbed in Abdomen, Robbed of Cellphone Near 37 Avenue

stories.title: Man Wounded in Daytime Shooting on Bay Parkway in Bath Beach
stories.dek: A 32-year-old man was shot in the hand and leg outside a Bath Beach building on Oct. 14, and police were searching for the gunman, amNY reported.
body: A 32-year-old man was shot and wounded in the early afternoon of Wednesday, Oct. 14, in front of 8817 Bay Parkway near Cropsey Avenue in Bath Beach, Brooklyn, according to police cited by amNY.
Police said the gunfire broke out at about 1:40 p.m. Officers from the 62nd Precinct responded after a 911 call and found the man with gunshot wounds to his left hand and left leg.
EMS took him to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn, where he was listed in stable condition, police sources told amNY.

Early in the investigation, police had not identified a motive or released a description of the shooter. Detectives were canvassing the area for video cameras that may have recorded the shooting, and no arrests had been made, according to the report.

The 62nd Precinct had recorded three shooting incidents this year through Oct. 11, one more than at the same point in 2025, according to NYPD statistics cited by amNY. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Brooklyn shooting: Man wounded in daytime attack near apartment building

stories.title: Man Stabbed After Argument on Uptown 6 Train Near Astor Place
stories.dek: A 40-year-old man suffered multiple stab wounds after a dispute aboard a 6 train in the East Village, and police were seeking a masked suspect, amNY reported.
body: A 40-year-old man was stabbed multiple times aboard an uptown 6 train near the Astor Place station in the East Village early Wednesday, Oct. 14, according to police sources cited by amNY.
The attack happened at about 2:25 a.m., the outlet reported. Officers from the 9th Precinct and NYPD Transit District 4 were alerted and found the wounded man after the train pulled into Astor Place.
EMS took the man to Bellevue Hospital, where he was listed in stable condition, according to the report.
A preliminary investigation found that the man had a verbal dispute with the suspect before the stabbing, police said. The cause of the argument was not known.

The suspect fled the station. Police described him as a man with a dark complexion who was wearing a ski mask. No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, according to amNY. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Manhattan subway stabbing: Man attacked after argument on 6 train in East Village, cops say

stories.title: Shooting Near Bed-Stuy School Prompts Shelter-in-Place
stories.dek: A person sitting in a car was shot in the leg at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue, leading a nearby school to shelter in place, News 12 Brooklyn reported.
body: A Bedford-Stuyvesant school was placed under a shelter-in-place on Tuesday, Oct. 13, after a shooting nearby, News 12 Brooklyn reported.

Police said the shooting happened just after 1 p.m. at the intersection of Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue, near P.S. 309, according to the outlet. The victim was shot in the right leg while sitting inside a car, News 12 reported. The article did not say exactly which school was placed under the order or when it began.
The victim was taken to Wyckoff Hospital for treatment. The report did not describe the person's condition, and it did not give the victim's name, age or gender.
School staff told News 12 that the shelter-in-place was lifted later in the day and that no students were hurt.
No arrests had been made at the time of the report, according to police. News 12 did not report a description of a suspect or a possible motive, and the investigation was continuing.

sources.title: Nearby shooting prompts shelter-in-place at Bed-Stuy school

stories.title: Man, 24, Stabbed on 2 Train Platform at East 180th Street Station
stories.dek: A 24-year-old man was stabbed Tuesday night on the northbound 2 train platform at the East 180th Street station in the Bronx, and no arrests had been made, Hoodline reported.
body: A 24-year-old man was stabbed on Tuesday night, Oct. 13, on the northbound 2 train platform at the East 180th Street station in the Bronx, police said, according to Hoodline.
The man was taken to a local hospital in stable condition, police said. PIX11, citing sources, reported that he had been uncooperative with investigators, according to Hoodline.
Detectives were searching for a suspect, and no arrests had been made as of Wednesday, the outlet reported. Police had not released a description of the attacker or announced any charges.

Hoodline noted several earlier incidents at the same station this year. In late July, a 45-year-old man was slashed in the neck after an argument on the northbound platform, and on Aug. 17 a 31-year-old commuter was slashed in the arm aboard a southbound 2 train, according to reports cited by the outlet. In late August, a 65-year-old woman was pushed onto the tracks from the 5 train platform; police rescued her and took a person of interest into custody, News 12 Bronx reported.

NYPD CompStat figures through Oct. 11 showed subway transit crime complaints up 1.6% year to date, according to Hoodline, which noted that no station-specific count was available. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: 24-Year-Old Stabbed at East 180th St Station in the Bronx

stories.title: Teen, 15, Slashed in Head During Melee in Flushing Meadows Corona Park
stories.dek: Police answering a shots-fired call near the New York Hall of Science on Oct. 12 found a large group and a 15-year-old boy with slash wounds, QNS reported.
body: A 15-year-old boy was slashed across the head and left arm during a melee involving a large, disorderly group inside Flushing Meadows Corona Park on the afternoon of Monday, Oct. 12, according to the NYPD as cited by QNS.

Officers from the 110th Precinct were dispatched just after 5 p.m. to reports of shots fired near 111th Street and 47th Avenue in Corona, close to the New York Hall of Science, the outlet reported. There they found the group in the park and then learned that the teenager had been hurt.
EMS took the boy to Harlem Hospital, where he was listed in stable condition, police said. According to police, EMS chose Harlem Hospital rather than Elmhurst Hospital, which is about two miles away.
Police said they were seeking both a gunman and a separate person who carried out the slashing. No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, according to QNS.

Through Oct. 11, the 110th Precinct had reported 550 felony assaults this year, up 15.1% from 478 at the same point last year, according to CompStat figures cited by the outlet. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Teenager slashed in head during melee involving a 'disorderly group' inside Flushing Meadows Corona Park: NYPD

stories.title: Far Rockaway Teen Charged With Murder in Killing of 14-Year-Old in Arverne
stories.dek: A 17-year-old was arraigned on a second-degree murder charge, accused of fatally shooting a 14-year-old boy at the Ocean Bay Apartments on Sept. 21, QNS reported.
body: A 17-year-old from Far Rockaway was arraigned Wednesday, Oct. 14, in Queens Supreme Court on charges of second-degree murder and two counts of second-degree criminal possession of a weapon in the fatal shooting of a 14-year-old boy in Arverne, according to QNS.

According to the criminal complaint cited by the outlet, the boy and three others arrived on push scooters at the courtyard of the Ocean Bay Apartments at about 3:33 p.m. on Sept. 21. Prosecutors allege the defendant approached the boy beside a residential building at 51-24 Beach Channel Drive and fired two shots.

One bullet struck the boy in the lower back, according to the complaint. EMS took him to Cohen Children's Medical Center in Glen Oaks, where he underwent emergency surgery and was later pronounced dead, QNS reported.

Prosecutors allege the teen then took the boy's scooter, fled east on Norton Avenue and changed clothes in a public bathroom. Police later recovered the clothing from a bathroom trash bin, according to the report.
Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz called the killing targeted and execution-style, the outlet reported.

Justice Seth Steed ordered the defendant held without bail and set a return date of Oct. 19, according to QNS. If convicted, he faces up to 25 years to life in prison. The charges are accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Far Rockaway teenager faces 25 years to life in prison for 'execution-style' murder of 14-year-old boy in Arverne: DA

stories.title: 12-Year-Old Girl Wounded in Bronx Shooting; Two Men Sought
stories.dek: A 12-year-old girl was shot in the torso and foot on Tratman Avenue in the Bronx on Monday night, and police were looking for two men, News 12 Bronx reported.
body: A 12-year-old girl was shot in the torso and right foot on Monday night, Oct. 12, outside 2465 Tratman Avenue near Rowland Street in the Bronx, according to News 12 Bronx.
The shooting happened at about 8:30 p.m., the outlet reported. Police sources told News 12 that the girl was not the intended target. It was not immediately clear who was.

The girl was taken to Montefiore Hospital by private means and was in stable condition, police said. The FDNY said she had already left the scene by the time its emergency medical crews arrived, according to the report.
Video from the scene showed a gun lying on the street beside a car tire, and roughly seven evidence markers for shell casings were visible as investigators collected evidence, News 12 reported.

Police sources said two men dressed in all black ran toward Zerega Avenue after the shooting. No arrests had been made at the time of the report, and police were still investigating what led to the gunfire.

sources.title: 12-year-old girl wounded in Bronx shooting; 2 men sought

stories.title: Rider Slashed in Face During Argument on 4 Train Near Grand Central
stories.dek: Police released images of a man they say slashed a 34-year-old rider across the face aboard a downtown 4 train on Oct. 8, amNY reported.
body: Police are searching for a man they say slashed a 34-year-old rider across the face aboard a downtown 4 train as it approached the 42nd Street-Grand Central station, according to amNY.

The attack happened at about 9:25 p.m. on Oct. 8, police said. According to the preliminary police account cited by the outlet, the two men got into a verbal dispute that turned into a physical struggle, and the suspect pulled out a sharp object and cut the victim.

The incident was reported to the Midtown South Precinct, and officers from NYPD Transit District 4 responded. EMS took the injured man to Bellevue Hospital in stable condition, according to the report.

The suspect fled in an unknown direction, police said. Investigators released images of him on Sunday night, Oct. 11, and described him as a man last seen wearing a black jacket, blue jeans and multicolored sneakers.
No arrests had been reported. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS or submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org, according to amNY.

sources.title: Grand Central subway slashing: Suspect sought for violently attacking man during argument on 4 train

stories.title: Teen Arrested in Armed Flushing Home Invasion; Three Others Sought
stories.dek: Police arrested a 17-year-old after four masked men forced their way into a Flushing home and robbed a 45-year-old man, QNS reported.
body: Police arrested a 17-year-old in connection with an armed home invasion in Flushing early Sunday, Oct. 11, and three other men remain at large, according to the NYPD as cited by QNS.

At about 2:30 a.m., four masked men forced their way into a residence on the Horace Harding Expressway near 150th Street, police said. Three of them displayed firearms and demanded the 45-year-old resident's property, while the fourth struck him in the face with a crowbar, leaving him with facial cuts, according to police.

The intruders took the man's watch and a chain, valued by police at about $65,000, then left him zip-tied and fled in an unknown direction, the outlet reported. The man declined medical attention at the scene.

Officers from the 109th Precinct arrested the 17-year-old nearby a short time later, police said. He was charged with robbery, assault, burglary, grand larceny, criminal trespass and harassment, and his arraignment in Queens Criminal Court was pending, according to QNS. The charges are accusations, and he is presumed innocent.
Police asked anyone with information about the three remaining suspects to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Teen busted after violent home invasion in Flushing; three armed accomplices remain at large: NYPD

stories.title: Queens Man Charged With Murder in Fatal Beating Outside Chelsea Adult Store
stories.dek: Police charged a 25-year-old Queens man with murder and robbery after a 60-year-old Pennsylvania man was beaten to death following an argument in a Chelsea store, amNY reported.
body: A 25-year-old Queens man has been charged with murder and two counts of robbery in the death of a 60-year-old Pennsylvania man who was beaten following an argument inside a Chelsea adult store on Sunday night, according to amNY.
Police identified the accused as Imani McColley, whose last known address was a homeless shelter in Jamaica, Queens, the outlet reported.

The confrontation began at about 9 p.m. inside Rainbow Station, an adult store at 203 Eighth Avenue, police said. According to police, the argument turned physical and spilled onto the street, where McColley allegedly shoved the man to the ground, stomped on him repeatedly, took his wallet and fled.

Officers from the 10th Precinct and paramedics responded to a 911 call reporting an assault in progress and found the man badly hurt. EMS took him to Bellevue Hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to the report.

Police sources told amNY that McColley returned to the scene later that night, and an eyewitness pointed him out to officers, who took him into custody. The killing appeared to be the 10th Precinct's first murder of the year, according to NYPD statistics cited by the outlet.
The charges are accusations, and McColley is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The article did not report a court appearance or plea.

sources.title: Sex shop murder: Queens man charged with fatally beating man during argument in Chelsea

stories.title: Flushing Man Charged With Manslaughter in Crash That Killed Baby in Stroller
stories.dek: Queens prosecutors say a 57-year-old driver was impaired by drugs when he ran a stop sign in Murray Hill and struck a stroller carrying a 1-year-old boy, QNS reported.
body: A 57-year-old Flushing man has been charged with manslaughter after prosecutors say he struck and killed a 1-year-old boy in a stroller while driving under the influence of drugs in Murray Hill, Queens, according to QNS.

Prosecutors identified the driver as Elvin Rivera of 150th Place. According to the charges, at about 8:35 a.m. on Sunday, Oct. 11, Rivera was driving a white 2016 Chevrolet Silverado north on Murray Street, rolled through the stop sign at 32nd Avenue, accelerated and hit the stroller in a marked crosswalk, the outlet reported.

The boy's 69-year-old nanny was pushing the stroller about three blocks from the child's home, according to the report. EMS took the boy to Jacobi Hospital in critical condition, where he was later pronounced dead. The nanny was taken to NewYork-Presbyterian Queens Hospital in stable condition with an arm injury.

Rivera remained at the scene and was taken into custody by 109th Precinct officers, QNS reported. Prosecutors said he failed a field sobriety test and that a roadside drug test detected cocaine and THC. The outlet noted he has an open DWI case in the Bronx from April.

He was arraigned Oct. 12 on charges including second-degree manslaughter, vehicular manslaughter and driving under the influence, pleaded not guilty and was ordered held without bail, according to the report. He is due back in court Oct. 19. Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz called the death completely avoidable. Rivera is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Flushing man charged with manslaughter for killing a baby in stroller while driving under influence of drugs: DA

stories.title: Pedestrian Critically Injured in Jamaica Avenue Hit-and-Run
stories.dek: A 54-year-old man was struck by a driver who fled on Jamaica Avenue near 184th Street early Sunday, amNY reported.
body: A 54-year-old man was critically injured early Sunday, Oct. 11, when a driver struck him on Jamaica Avenue near 184th Street in Queens and fled, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The crash happened at about 1:51 a.m., the outlet reported. Police said the man was crossing Jamaica Avenue from the northwest corner to the southwest corner when an eastbound gray Ford Crown Victoria hit him.
The man suffered serious head and body injuries, police said. EMS took him to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where he was listed in critical condition, according to the report.
The driver did not remain at the scene and continued east on Jamaica Avenue, police said. No arrests had been made at the time of publication.

The NYPD Highway District Investigation Squad is leading the investigation, amNY reported. Police asked anyone with information to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

sources.title: Pedestrian left fighting for his life after Queens hit-and-run: cops

stories.title: Man Arrested After Two Slashed, Standoff at Far Rockaway Building
stories.dek: Police said a 52-year-old man slashed a man and a woman at a Beach 54th Street apartment building and then barricaded himself inside, ABC7 New York reported.
body: A 52-year-old man was taken into custody after police said he slashed two people at an apartment building on Beach 54th Street in Far Rockaway, Queens, and then barricaded himself inside, according to ABC7 New York.
The attack happened just before midnight, the station reported. Its article, published Saturday, Oct. 10, did not give the calendar date of the incident.
A man and a woman were injured in the slashing, according to authorities cited by ABC7. Both were expected to recover.

Officers responded to the building, where the suspect had barricaded himself after the attack, police said. During the response, one officer fired a weapon, but no one was struck by the gunfire, authorities said. The article did not say what led the officer to fire.

Police said the suspect was eventually taken into custody. His name was not released, and the station reported no information about charges, bail or a court date. The victims were not identified, and authorities said additional details were not immediately available. The suspect is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Man arrested after slashing 2 people, barricading himself in Queens

stories.title: Stapleton Man Charged After Allegedly Booting Car Blocking His Driveway
stories.dek: Police say a Staten Island man put a wheel boot on a Jeep parked across his Waverly Place driveway and demanded $25, then was found carrying a stun gun, Hoodline reported.
body: A 52-year-old Stapleton man has been charged after police say he put a wheel boot on a car blocking his driveway on Waverly Place and left a note demanding $25 to remove it, according to Hoodline.

The man, identified as Aaron Hardy, allegedly attached the boot to the front left tire of a gray 2015 Jeep Compass on Oct. 2 near Targee Street, according to a criminal complaint cited by silive.com. The driver had parked at about 7:30 a.m. and found the boot around 3 p.m., the reports said.

Hardy told police he had paperwork authorizing him to boot the car and that 311 had told him he could, according to the reports. Gothamist reported that the city has no provision allowing residents to boot other people's cars without a license. Police said Hardy removed the boot himself with a key, and officers found an electronic stun gun in his waistband when they arrested him.

He faces charges including felony criminal possession of a weapon, third-degree coercion, attempted petit larceny and criminal tampering, according to silive.com and Gothamist. Hardy pleaded not guilty and was released on non-monetary conditions.

His attorney, Kelvin Richards, said Hardy is innocent and will fight the charges, while acknowledging that he booted the car, the reports said. Richards said the driver had interfered with Hardy's car wash and repair business. Hardy is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Stapleton Man Boots Neighbor's Jeep Over Driveway, Cops Find Stun Gun on Him

stories.title: Teen Stabbed and Beaten With Bat Near Crown Heights School; Five Sought
stories.dek: A 16-year-old boy was stabbed and struck with a bat on President Street in Crown Heights, and police were searching for five suspects, amNY reported.
body: A 16-year-old boy was stabbed and beaten with a bat in front of an apartment building at 993 President Street in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, just before 10 a.m. Friday, Oct. 9, according to police cited by amNY.

Police said five males confronted the teen and a verbal dispute followed. The attack escalated when he tried to run away, according to police. Law enforcement sources told amNY that one suspect stabbed the teen in the back while another struck his legs and knees several times with a bat.

The teen ran about a block to the Prospect Heights High School Campus on Classon Avenue, where School Safety Agents helped him and called police, sources said. Officers from the 71st Precinct responded to the school.
EMS took the boy to Maimonides Medical Center, where he was listed in stable condition, the outlet reported.

The suspects were last seen running west on President Street. No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, police said. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Teenager stabbed and beaten with bat near Brooklyn high school; five suspects wanted, cops say

stories.title: Ozone Park Man Charged With Sex Abuse of Girl; Police Seek Other Victims
stories.dek: A 72-year-old Queens man was arrested on sex abuse charges involving a 12-year-old girl, and detectives said he may have other victims, amNY reported.
body: A 72-year-old Ozone Park man has been charged with sexually abusing a 12-year-old girl, and police said they believe he may have attacked others, according to amNY.

Police identified the accused as Nazim Uddin of 75th Street. According to police sources, the alleged abuse took place at about 7 p.m. on Sept. 8 inside a commercial establishment near 75th Street and 101st Avenue, not far from his home. The article did not say whether he worked at the business or what connection, if any, he had to the girl.

Members of the Queens Child Abuse Squad arrested Uddin on the afternoon of Oct. 8, about a month after the incident, the outlet reported. He was booked on charges of sexual abuse and acting in a manner injurious to a child.

Based on a preliminary investigation, special victims detectives believe there may be additional victims, police said. The NYPD issued an alert Thursday night asking anyone who may have been harmed by him to come forward.

Court records indicated Uddin was scheduled for arraignment in Queens Criminal Court on Friday, Oct. 9, amNY reported; the outcome was not reported. The charges are accusations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police asked anyone with information to call the NYPD Sex Crimes Hotline at 212-267-7273 or Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Queens man charged with sex abuse of 12-year-old girl may have other victims: cops

stories.title: Teen Fatally Shot at Harlem Housing Complex; Person of Interest Questioned
stories.dek: A 15-year-old boy was killed and a 57-year-old bystander wounded in a shooting at King Towers in Harlem, and detectives were questioning a person of interest, amNY reported.
body: A 15-year-old boy was fatally shot and a 57-year-old man was wounded at the King Towers public housing complex at 40 West 115th Street in Harlem just after 6:20 p.m. Wednesday, Oct. 7, according to the NYPD as cited by amNY.

Officers from the 28th Precinct and NYPD Public Service Area 5 responded after a ShotSpotter activation, police said. They found the teenager, a resident of King Towers, with a gunshot wound to the stomach. EMS took him to Mount Sinai Morningside Hospital in critical condition, where he died a short time later.

The 57-year-old man was struck in the right hand, police said. Investigators determined he was a bystander hit by a stray bullet. He was taken to Harlem Hospital in stable condition, according to the report.

Police took a person of interest into custody during the preliminary investigation, and charges were pending the outcome of the inquiry, amNY reported. As of Thursday morning, the motive was unknown, and sources said detectives were looking into whether the teen was the intended target.
Through Oct. 4, the 28th Precinct had recorded three homicides this year, down from five a year earlier, according to NYPD statistics cited by the outlet.

sources.title: Harlem shooting: Person of interest questioned in killing of teen at public housing complex

stories.title: Police Identify Man Killed in Mount Eden Stabbing, Release Suspect Image
stories.dek: A 27-year-old man died after being stabbed inside a Grand Concourse building in Mount Eden, and police released an image of a man they want to question, News 12 Bronx reported.
body: Police have identified a 27-year-old man who was fatally stabbed inside a building at 1555 Grand Concourse in the Mount Eden section of the Bronx, according to News 12 Bronx.

The stabbing happened just after 1:50 p.m. on Wednesday afternoon, the outlet reported. Investigators said the man suffered stab wounds to his neck. He was taken to Lincoln Hospital, where he died of his injuries.

Police released a new image of a man they want in connection with the killing, News 12 reported. He was last seen wearing a gray sweatshirt, a black jacket, black and red pants, and gray and white sneakers. Police did not identify him.
No arrests had been reported, and the investigation remained active, according to the outlet. The report did not describe a motive or say whether the two men knew each other.
Police asked anyone with information about the stabbing or the man in the image to contact them. Tips can be submitted to NYPD Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Mount Eden fatal stabbing victim identified

stories.title: Federal Immigration Agents Shoot and Wound Man in Marble Hill
stories.dek: Federal agents shot and injured a man during an attempted arrest at West 225th Street and Marble Hill Avenue, drawing protests and demands for answers from city and state officials, amNY reported.
body: Federal agents shot and wounded a man at about 4 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 8, at West 225th Street and Marble Hill Avenue in the Bronx, according to law enforcement sources cited by amNY. Multiple outlets identified the agents as ICE officers, and PIX11 reported the shooting likely happened during an attempted arrest.

The NYPD said the shooting involved federal agents and that city police were not involved or on scene at the time. A 5-year-old child was in the back seat of the man's car and was not hurt, ABC7 reported, which Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed. The man, whose name was not released, was being treated at NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital.

The Department of Homeland Security said hours later that agents were arresting a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior grand larceny conviction and that ICE officers rendered aid, amNY reported. DHS did not explain why an agent fired. Sources told the outlet that NYPD officers drove the man to the hospital.

Mamdani called the shooting unconscionable and said he called President Trump to demand an end to ICE enforcement in the city. Gov. Kathy Hochul said she spoke with Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and demanded the release of body camera footage, according to the report. U.S. Rep. Adriano Espaillat said agents denied him access to the man at the hospital.

Residents gathered at the scene, and protesters later assembled outside Allen Hospital, where clashes broke out with NYPD officers, amNY reported. The New York Immigration Coalition called for an independent investigation led by the state attorney general.

sources.title: ICE agents shoot and wound man in Marble Hill, leaving community and officials outraged

stories.title: Bronx Man Charged With Murder in Stabbing Death in Jamaica Park
stories.dek: Police charged a 53-year-old Bronx man with murder after a homeless man was fatally stabbed in Major Mark Park in Jamaica, Queens, QNS reported.
body: A 53-year-old Bronx man has been charged with murder in the fatal stabbing of a homeless man in Major Mark Park in Jamaica, Queens, on Wednesday morning, Oct. 7, according to the NYPD as cited by QNS.

Officers from the 103rd Precinct responded at 4:45 a.m. to a 911 call reporting an assault in progress inside the park, across from an apartment building at 87-70 173rd Street, police said. They found a man with two stab wounds to the chest, and EMS pronounced him dead at the scene. Investigators believe he was in his 30s; his name was withheld pending family notification.
According to a law enforcement source cited by the outlet, police canvassed the area with a witness, who recognized a man walking several blocks away. He was first detained as a person of interest.

Police identified him as Abdullah Spencerel of Ogden Avenue in Highbridge. He was formally arrested nearly eight hours later, after several witnesses said they saw him arguing with the victim before the stabbing, QNS reported. He was charged with murder and criminal possession of a weapon.

An NYPD spokesman could not say what the argument was about. Spencerel was expected to be arraigned in Queens Criminal Court on Thursday, according to the report. The charges are accusations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Bronx man accused of stabbing a homeless man to death in Major Mark Park in Jamaica: NYPD

stories.title: Queens Student, 15, Taken Into Custody After Gun Found in Backpack
stories.dek: A 15-year-old was detained at a Queens Village high school campus after a staff member spotted a handgun in his backpack following a fight, amNY reported.
body: A 15-year-old student was taken into police custody Wednesday afternoon, Oct. 7, after a handgun was found in his backpack at a high school campus in Queens Village, according to police sources cited by amNY.

Police were called just after 1 p.m. to the building at 230-17 Hillside Avenue, which houses Martin Van Buren High School and Business Technology Early College High School, the outlet reported. Officers from the 105th Precinct responded.
According to police sources, two boys had gotten into a fight inside the building. Afterward, a staff member spotted a 9mm handgun in one of the boys' backpacks, the report said.
School Safety agents held the student until police officers arrived, according to amNY.

Charges were pending the outcome of an ongoing investigation, law enforcement sources told the outlet. The article did not say whether anyone was injured in the fight or describe the status of the second boy. Neither student was identified.

sources.title: Queens student arrested after bringing gun to high school

stories.title: Former Midtown Attorney Faces New Charges in Sexual Assault Case
stories.dek: Manhattan prosecutors announced new charges against Ryan Hemphill, accusing the former attorney of sexually assaulting a seventh woman in his Midtown apartment, amNY reported.
body: Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced new charges on Tuesday, Oct. 6, against Ryan Hemphill, a 44-year-old former attorney accused of sexually assaulting a seventh woman in his Midtown apartment, according to amNY.
Prosecutors allege the newly charged assault took place in spring 2024 and lasted about seven hours, the outlet reported. Hemphill returned to court on Oct. 6.

Hemphill was indicted in 2025 on accusations that he assaulted six women between October 2024 and March 2025, according to the report. The current 41-count indictment in state Supreme Court includes nine counts of predatory sexual assault, multiple rape counts, first-degree aggravated sexual assault and second-degree assault, among other charges.

According to court documents cited by amNY, Hemphill met the woman through a dating website. Prosecutors also allege he pressured victims into recording statements saying the encounters were consensual.

body: A 25-year-old Bronx man has been arraigned on a second-degree murder charge in the fatal stabbing of a 59-year-old man aboard a Queens-bound J train, according to the office of Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz.

Prosecutors identified the accused as Jyrell Thomas. According to the charges, he boarded the train at Broadway Junction in Brooklyn at about 5 p.m. on Sept. 30. At about 5:15 p.m., as the train approached the elevated Woodhaven Boulevard station near Jamaica Avenue, he allegedly yelled, pulled out a knife and repeatedly stabbed the man, whom he did not know, the DA's office said.

When the doors opened, Thomas allegedly ran and dropped his weapon, prosecutors said. Passengers chased him, and NYPD officers responding to 911 calls arrested him two blocks away, where he had climbed onto a garage. Police recovered two kitchen knives, according to the release. The victim was taken to a hospital and pronounced dead.
Katz said New Yorkers deserve to ride transit without fear and thanked the passengers who pursued the attacker and the officers who made the arrest, according to the release.

Thomas also faces two counts of fourth-degree criminal possession of a weapon. Queens Criminal Court Judge Indira D. Khan ordered him held and set a return date of Oct. 6. If convicted, he faces up to 25 years to life in prison. The charges are accusations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

stories.title: Washington Heights Shelter Resident Charged in Fatal Stabbing
stories.dek: A 29-year-old resident of the Fort Washington Men's Shelter was charged with murder after a 33-year-old man was fatally stabbed during an argument inside the facility, amNY reported.
body: A 29-year-old resident of a Washington Heights homeless shelter has been charged with murder after a man was fatally stabbed during an argument inside the facility, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The stabbing happened just before noon on Sept. 27 inside the Fort Washington Men's Shelter at 651 West 168th Street, the outlet reported. Officers from the 33rd Precinct responded to a 911 call reporting an argument and a stabbing.

Police found a 33-year-old man with multiple stab wounds to his chest. EMS took him to Harlem Hospital in critical condition, where he later died, according to the report. His name was withheld pending family notification.
Police identified the accused as Javed Tyghter. He was taken into custody and charged with murder, police sources said. The article did not report a court date or plea.

According to the shelter's website, the facility houses 200 men dealing with mental health and substance use disorders, amNY reported. The outlet said the killing was the first reported murder in the 33rd Precinct this year. The charges are accusations, and Tyghter is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Washington Heights homeless shelter tenant charged with stabbing man to death during argument

stories.title: Police Say Woman Killed Near Central Park Boathouse Was Beaten With Stick
stories.dek: Detectives charged a 36-year-old man with murder in the death of a 63-year-old woman found in a gazebo near the Central Park Boathouse, and revised their account of how she died, amNY reported.
body: A 36-year-old man has been charged with murder and criminal possession of a weapon in the death of a 63-year-old woman found in a wooden gazebo near the Boathouse in Central Park on Sunday morning, Sept. 27, according to police cited by amNY.

Police said the woman was found unconscious with a head injury at 9:43 a.m. near East 74th Street and East Drive. Officers from the Central Park Precinct and EMS responded, and EMS pronounced her dead at about 10 a.m. Her name was withheld pending family notification.
Police had initially reported that she had stab wounds, but they now say the accused beat her with a wooden stick, the outlet reported.
Detectives identified the accused as Jonathan Robles, who is homeless and has an address listed at the Barbour Hotel shelter in Hell's Kitchen, according to the report.

The woman is believed to have been homeless and living in the area, with a tent and belongings near the gazebo, amNY reported. Sources described her as a known artist who sold her paintings there. Detectives sealed off the area and examined it in heavy rain.
The charges are accusations, and Robles is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.title: Central Park murder: Homeless man charged with fatally beating woman with stick near Boathouse

stories.title: Man Fatally Shot Outside Astoria Club in Apparent Robbery Attempt
stories.dek: A 45-year-old man was shot in the back during a struggle with a gunman who tried to take his jewelry outside a Steinway Street club, amNY reported.
body: A 45-year-old man was shot and killed outside the Riviera Gentleman's Club at 34-48 Steinway Street in Astoria, Queens, at about 3:45 a.m. Thursday, Sept. 24, in what police called an apparent robbery attempt, according to amNY.

A preliminary investigation found that the gunman approached the man from behind and tried to take his jewelry, police sources said. During a struggle, the gunman fired, striking the man in the back, according to police.
The gunman ran, got into an SUV and drove off along 35th Avenue, police said. Investigators do not believe he took any of the man's belongings. The outlet did not report a description of the suspect.

Officers from the 114th Precinct and EMS responded, and the man was taken to Elmhurst Hospital in critical condition, where he died, the report said. His name was withheld pending family notification.

No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing. Murders in the 114th Precinct have doubled this year, from two at this point last year to four, according to NYPD data cited by amNY. Tips can be shared with Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Man shot to death outside Queens strip club in apparent robbery attempt: cops

stories.title: Man, 24, Fatally Shot in Downtown Brooklyn Park; Two Men Sought
stories.dek: A 24-year-old Brownsville man was shot to death in McLaughlin Park after an argument with two men, who remain at large, amNY reported.
body: A 24-year-old man from Brownsville was shot and killed inside McLaughlin Park in Downtown Brooklyn on Tuesday afternoon, Sept. 22, and police are searching for two men seen confronting him, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The NYPD received a 911 call at about 2:07 p.m., the outlet reported. Officers from the 84th Precinct found the man with gunshot wounds to the stomach. EMS took him to NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital in critical condition, where he was pronounced dead.
Witnesses told investigators that the man had been seen arguing with two other men before the shooting, according to the report. What the argument was about was not clear.

Police said one of the two men was last seen wearing a gray Nike Tech suit and carrying a black backpack, and the other was wearing a green Nike Tech suit. After the shooting, they reportedly ran north on Flatbush Avenue and then east toward Concord Street.

No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, according to amNY. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

sources.title: Man shot to death in Downtown Brooklyn Park identified, two suspects on the loose

stories.title: Teen Fatally Shot in Arverne; Gunman Fled on Victim's Scooter, Sources Say
stories.dek: A 14-year-old boy was shot during an attempted robbery behind the Ocean Bay Apartments in Arverne, and police released an image of the suspect, amNY reported.
body: A 14-year-old boy was shot and killed behind the Ocean Bay Apartments at 51-24 Beach Channel Drive in Arverne, Queens, just after 5:30 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21, according to police sources cited by amNY. The outlet reported that he lived a few blocks away.
Police said the boy was riding his scooter when a man approached and tried to rob him. The boy resisted, and the gunman shot him in the lower back, according to police.

The shooter then took the boy's scooter and fled east on Beach 52nd Street, police said, and was last seen riding east along Norton Avenue. Sources confirmed to the outlet that the scooter was used to get away.
The shooting was reported to the 101st Precinct. EMS took the boy to Cohen Children's Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, according to the report.

On Tuesday, the NYPD released an image of the suspect, described as a male with a dark complexion last seen wearing a black hooded sweatshirt, black and gray pants, and red and white sneakers. No arrests had been made as of publication, and the investigation was continuing. Through Sept. 20, the 101st Precinct had recorded five homicides this year, up from three a year earlier, amNY reported. Tips can be shared with Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Queens shooting: Suspect who shot teen dead fled on victim's own scooter, sources said

stories.title: Mother and Son Shot While Doing Laundry in Allerton
stories.dek: A 37-year-old woman and her 17-year-old son were each shot in the leg inside a laundromat on Astor Avenue in the Bronx, amNY reported.
body: A 37-year-old woman and her 17-year-old son were shot while washing clothes inside the Astor Laundromat at 760 Astor Avenue in the Allerton section of the Bronx at about 7:15 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21, according to police sources cited by amNY.
Officers from the 49th Precinct responded to a 911 call reporting gunfire inside the laundromat, police said. They found the mother and son each with a gunshot wound to the right leg.
Officers gave first aid until EMS arrived, the outlet reported. EMS took both to Jacobi Hospital, where they were listed in stable condition.

Police did not immediately have a description of the gunman. Investigators were looking into whether the two were the intended targets or were struck by gunfire aimed at someone else, according to the report. As of Tuesday morning, the motive was not known.

No arrests had been made as of publication, amNY reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X, where tips are kept confidential.

sources.title: Mother and son shot inside of Bronx laundromat

stories.title: Man, 60, Beaten and Slashed Outside Kingsbridge Apartment Building
stories.dek: A 60-year-old man was struck from behind and slashed with a box cutter outside a Sedgwick Avenue building in the Bronx, police sources told amNY.
body: A 60-year-old man was beaten and slashed in what police described as an unprovoked attack outside an apartment building at 2710 Sedgwick Avenue in the Kingsbridge section of the Bronx at about 8:43 a.m. Monday, Sept. 21, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The man was standing outside the building talking with another person when the attacker approached from behind and struck him with an unknown blunt object, law enforcement sources said. Police said the attacker then pulled out a box cutter, cut the man on the neck and ran off in an unknown direction.

Officers from the 50th Precinct and EMS responded. Paramedics took the man to St. Barnabas Hospital with a head injury and a cut on the left side of his neck, and he was listed in stable condition, according to the report.
Police said the attacker was last seen wearing a green baseball cap, a blue coat and light-colored pants.

No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, the outlet reported. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit a tip at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

sources.title: Man beaten, slashed in unprovoked Bronx attack: cops

stories.title: 14-Year-Old Boy Critically Wounded in Far Rockaway Shooting
stories.dek: A 14-year-old boy was shot in the back near Beach Channel Drive on Monday afternoon, and police were seeking a male who fled on a scooter, amNY reported.
body: A 14-year-old boy was shot in the back near 51-24 Beach Channel Drive in Far Rockaway, Queens, at about 3:36 p.m. Monday, Sept. 21, according to police sources cited by amNY.

The boy was walking in the area when shots were fired, police sources said. Officers from the 101st Precinct responded, and EMS took him to Cohen Children's Medical Center. The outlet described him as critically wounded and reported that he was listed in serious condition.
Investigators were looking into whether the boy was shot during a possible attempt to rob him of his scooter, according to police sources.
Authorities said they wanted to question a male who was last seen leaving on a scooter, wearing a black sweatshirt and white shorts.

No arrests had been made and the investigation was continuing, according to the report. Police asked the public to stay away from the area while they worked the scene. Anyone with information was asked to call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS, submit tips at crimestoppers.nypdonline.org or message @NYPDTips on X.

sources.title: Queens shooting leaves 14-year-old boy fighting for his life, cops say
